title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the Provisions on the Administration of the Construction of People's Courts' Computer Information Network Systems and the Plan for the Construction of People's Courts' Computer Information Network Systems
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Issuing the Administrative Provisions on the Construction of Computer Information Network Systems of People's Courts and the Plan for the Construction of Computer Information Network Systems of People's Courts

Fa Fa [2002] No. 4

High People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; and the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

The Administrative Provisions on the Construction of Computer Information Network Systems of People's Courts and the Plan for the Construction of Computer Information Network Systems of People's Courts are hereby issued to you for compliance.

People's courts at all levels shall, in accordance with the Administrative Provisions on the Construction of Computer Information Network Systems of People's Courts and the administrative provisions formulated by higher-level courts, and taking into account local circumstances, formulate relevant rules and regulations for the management and use of their own computer information network systems, so as to ensure the secure operation of the computer network system and maximize its effectiveness. All high people's courts shall, in accordance with the requirements of the Plan for the Construction of Computer Information Network Systems of People's Courts and taking into account local conditions, formulate specific plans and implementation schemes for the construction of computer information network systems for courts at all levels within their respective jurisdictions, and issue them for implementation simultaneously.

January 29, 2002

Administrative Provisions on the Construction of Computer Information Network Systems of People's Courts

Article 1. These Provisions are formulated in accordance with relevant documents such as the Supreme People's Court's Outline of the Five-Year Reform of People's Courts (Fa Fa [1999] No. 28), the Material Construction Plan for People's Courts during the National Tenth Five-Year Plan Period (Fa Fa [2001] No. 15), and the Plan for the Construction of Computer Information Network Systems of People's Courts, for the purpose of strengthening the management of the construction of computer information network systems of people's courts.

Article 2. The computer information network system of a people's court is a computer information system constructed by the people's court in accordance with the needs of adjudication work and other work of the court, for the purposes of improving management level, standardizing adjudication procedures, enhancing work efficiency, and ensuring work quality. This system includes the construction of local area networks (LANs) and wide area networks (WANs) in people's courts at all levels nationwide using computer technology and communication technology, as well as the use of computer network technology to assist in the management of adjudication work and other work.

Article 3. The construction of computer information network systems of people's courts shall adhere to the purpose of serving the theme of "justice and efficiency" for people's courts in the 21st century, serving adjudication work, serving leadership decision-making, and serving the management of all work of people's courts. It shall provide advanced management tools for adjudication work and other work of people's courts, and gradually realize the modernization of office work, case handling, and other management work of people's courts.

Article 4. The Supreme People's Court is the information center and network management center of the national court computer information network system. Each high people's court is the information center and network management center of the court computer information network system of its province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government. Each intermediate people's court is the information center and network management center of the computer information network system of its city (prefecture, autonomous prefecture). Each basic people's court is a basic-level user unit of the court network system. Basic people's courts with the necessary conditions may construct independent computer LANs and computer WANs connecting their dispatched people's tribunals. To ensure smooth network operation, implement effective network management, and facilitate the training of technical personnel, network equipment and system databases must comply with the unified technical standards required by the document National Court Computer Information Network Construction Plan (Fa [1996] No. 54).

Article 5. The ultimate purpose of constructing computer information network systems of people's courts is to achieve the practical application of modern science and technology, such as computers, in adjudication work and other work. People's courts at all levels shall overcome the tendency to emphasize construction but neglect application and overlook management, and shall formulate effective management measures to ensure system application and realize system benefits.

During the operation of computer information network systems of people's courts at all levels, there must be system administrators, system database administrators, system security administrators, internal website administrators, and other sufficient full-time technical personnel. In people's courts with smaller network scales, technical personnel may hold multiple positions concurrently.

Article 6. For the construction of computer information networks of people's courts at all levels, the system functions shall first be determined, the network scale shall be determined based on the functional requirements, and system application software shall be selected. The system hardware configuration shall be determined based on the requirements of the system application software.

Article 7. The hardware part of the computer information network system of a people's court includes application servers (dual-machine hot standby), file and print servers, internal website servers, mail servers, video-on-demand servers, network security servers, network management workstations, network equipment, desktop computers, and other equipment. The application servers of high people's courts and intermediate and basic people's courts with favorable economic conditions shall install minicomputers and adopt dual-machine hot standby technology, using the UNIX network operating system. The application servers of intermediate and basic people's courts in less economically developed regions may use high-end microcomputers and install the NT network operating system.

Article 8. The basic functions, business flow modes, data exchange with higher and lower courts, basic data structures, judicial statistics interfaces, standard code tables, domain names, IP addresses, etc., of network application software developed or used by people's courts at all levels must comply with the technical standards for national court computer network construction formulated by the Supreme People's Court, and must be able to automatically fill in the judicial statistics case management information table. People's courts that have already constructed computer information network systems may upgrade and modify their application software in accordance with the requirements of the technical standards for national court computer network construction. People's courts that have not yet constructed network systems may use network application software recommended by the Supreme People's Court, or may develop software themselves in accordance with the technical standards formulated by the Supreme People's Court. Courts at all levels should avoid low-level duplicate development as much as possible, which would waste human, financial, and time resources.

Article 9. The functions of the application software system shall be complete, advanced, practical, and stable. Mature and advanced technologies shall be adopted to ensure the comprehensive application of computer network management technology in adjudication work and other work. At the same time, in accordance with changes and developments in court work, the application software system shall have scalability and ease of maintenance.

Article 10. The construction of computer information network systems of people's courts shall fully consider the needs of court trials, connecting the computer information system with the equipment used by judges in the trial court to meet the judges' requirements for accessing and querying relevant information and materials during trials.

The construction of computer information network systems of people's courts shall fully consider the needs of court work, connecting them with video conferencing systems and communication systems, to meet the needs for the transmission, storage, development, and use of trial information materials, laws and regulations information materials, image information materials, and other information materials within the court system.

Article 11. The construction of computer information network systems of people's courts shall pay special attention to system security. When constructing communication and computer information systems, people's courts at all levels must simultaneously construct confidentiality facilities. Such systems may only be put into use after being reported to and approved by the confidentiality department at the same level. Safety and confidentiality equipment must use products recommended by the State Secrets Bureau (including network security inspection, network security prevention, network security isolation, electromagnetic leakage inspection, electromagnetic leakage prevention, etc.). In accordance with the requirements of the state confidentiality department, computer LANs and WANs used internally within courts must be physically isolated from the externally connected Internet.

Article 12. The system application software shall have necessary security measures to ensure that data is not illegally viewed, modified, or deleted. To ensure the integrity and security of system operation data, the system must have an operation log that sequentially records various data of computers accessing the network.

Article 13. To improve system reliability, the system shall have real-time data backup functions. Data shall also be regularly backed up using tapes, optical discs, etc., to prevent data loss. Major network equipment shall have a certain proportion of redundancy.

Article 14. The construction plan for the computer information network system of a people's court at any level must be approved before implementation. Construction plans of people's courts at all levels shall be reported level by level up to the high people's court. The high people's court shall decide, based on the circumstances, whether to report to the Supreme People's Court for approval.

The Supreme People's Court is responsible for approving the construction plans of high people's courts, intermediate people's courts of cities with separate planning status, and intermediate people's courts of provincial capitals (capitals of autonomous regions). The construction plans of other courts are subject to approval by the respective high people's courts. Construction plans for computer information network systems already approved during the Ninth Five-Year Plan period need not be re-approved.

Article 15. After a computer information network system of a people's court at any level is completed and has been in operation for six months, an acceptance check may be applied for, and a WAN connection to the national court computer information network system may be established. Courts at all levels shall submit their acceptance check applications level by level up to the high people's court. The high people's court shall decide, based on the circumstances, whether to report to the Supreme People's Court for acceptance.

The Supreme People's Court is responsible for accepting completed computer information network systems of high people's courts, intermediate people's courts of cities with separate planning status, and intermediate people's courts of provincial capitals (capitals of autonomous regions). The computer information network systems of other courts are subject to acceptance by the respective high people's courts.

Article 16. The basis for examining and approving the plans for computer information network systems of people's courts includes the unified technical standards required by the Supreme People's Court, such as basic functions, business flow modes, data exchange with higher and lower courts, basic data structures, standard code tables, as well as management measures such as WAN connection dedicated line methods, system operation reports, system security measures, and system application.

Article 17. For WAN interconnection between the Supreme People's Court and high people's courts, a 2M "three networks in one" dedicated line for data, voice, and image shall be adopted. The method of WAN interconnection from each high people's court to intermediate people's courts shall be determined by the respective high people's court based on actual circumstances and reported to the Supreme People's Court for record. The method of WAN interconnection from each intermediate people's court to basic people's courts shall be determined by the respective intermediate people's court based on actual circumstances and reported to the high people's court for record. High people's courts shall strengthen their guidance to lower courts regarding the construction of computer information network systems.

When selecting WAN connection methods, high people's courts and intermediate people's courts with favorable economic conditions shall fully consider the requirements for dedicated line communication and video transmission needed in court work.

Article 18. People's courts at all levels shall strengthen the management of website construction. The construction of a website by a high people's court shall be reported to the Supreme People's Court for approval. The construction of a website by an intermediate people's court or a basic people's court shall be reported to the high people's court for approval. Existing websites shall submit a supplementary report in accordance with the above provisions.

Article 19. These Provisions shall take effect from the date of issuance.

Article 20. The interpretation of these Provisions shall be the responsibility of the Supreme People's Court.

Plan for the Construction of Computer Information Network Systems of People's Courts

With the implementation of the strategy of governing the country according to law and the continuous development of information technology, the construction of computer information network systems of people's courts faces new opportunities and challenges. Serving the theme of "justice and efficiency" is the fundamental function of the construction and application of computer information network systems of people's courts. Establishing an efficient, coordinated, and standardized working mechanism and management system, and further improving work quality and efficiency, are important tasks for the construction of computer information network systems of people's courts. People's courts at all levels must fully recognize the importance and urgency of accelerating the construction of computer information network systems of people's courts, take practical measures, and make full use of modern scientific technologies such as network technology, computer technology, and modern communication technology to accelerate the pace of constructing computer information network systems of people's courts.

To accelerate the process of constructing computer information network systems of people's courts, in accordance with the requirements of the Material Construction Plan for People's Courts during the National Tenth Five-Year Plan Period (Fa Fa [2001] No. 15) and with reference to the Outline of the National Government System E-Government Construction Plan 2001-2005, the Plan for the Construction of Computer Information Network Systems of People's Courts is formulated.

I. Current Status of the System

During the Ninth Five-Year Plan period, in accordance with the requirements of the National Court Computer Information Network Construction Plan (Fa [1996] No. 54) and the Interim Provisions on the Administration of the Construction of National Court Computer Information Networks (Trial Implementation) (Fa [1996] No. 55), and through the active efforts of people's courts at all levels, significant progress was made in the construction of computer information networks within the national court system:

1. The construction of computer information networks of national courts unified network equipment, databases, and code tables, providing convenient and practical basic conditions for WAN interconnection and network management.

2. Eight high people's courts, namely those of Beijing, Liaoning, Shanghai, Jiangsu, Fujian, Henan, Guangdong, and Hainan, completed the construction of their own computer LANs during the Ninth Five-Year Plan period, realizing information-based management of court adjudication work and other work represented by "trial procedure management," greatly improving work efficiency and quality. The WAN interconnection of the court systems in Beijing, Shanghai, and other places realized networked case handling, electronic information management, and, in part, paperless distribution of certain documents. These efforts accumulated rich experience for the construction of computer information network systems of national courts.

3. The above-listed eight high people's courts, as well as the high and intermediate people's courts of Tianjin, Jilin, Shandong, Sichuan, Nanjing, Qingdao, Dalian, Chengdu, and Harbin, actively developed court computer network application software, laying a solid foundation for the establishment of various technical standards for computer information network construction of people's courts.

4. During the Ninth Five-Year Plan period, approximately 300 computer LANs were built in courts nationwide. The establishment and widespread use of these court computer networks enabled court cadres and police to generally master modern case handling and office skills, enhanced their awareness of informatization, and continuously improved the level of office and case handling automation and management informatization, promoting the transformation of leadership methods and working methods. A professional team has begun to form, consisting of personnel who are both proficient in information technology and familiar with court work business.

However, on the whole, the construction of computer information networks of national courts still does not meet the requirements of China's economic and social development and the informatization of court work. The main problems are as follows: First, some court leaders do not fully recognize the importance and urgency of constructing computer information networks of people's courts and have not given them due attention. Second, a complete set of technical standards for network construction has not yet been formed within the national court system. Third, the phenomenon of low-level duplicate development of application software still exists, resulting in a waste of human and financial resources. Fourth, management norms are inconsistent, and safety and confidentiality systems are not well established. Fifth, development is unbalanced, with significant differences between the eastern, central, and western regions.

II. Overall Objectives

Based on China's national conditions and the characteristics of people's court work, the overall objectives of the construction of computer information network systems of national courts during the Tenth Five-Year Plan period are: People's courts at all levels shall construct computer LANs to carry out trial procedure management, trial auxiliary management, judicial archive management, judicial statistics management, office and judicial administrative management, etc., gradually realizing computerized management of adjudication work and various other work of people's courts. The national court system shall construct computer WANs to realize the exchange of trial information and other management information and resource sharing. Courts with the necessary conditions may explore the realization of functions such as remote document retrieval and evidence collection, and cross-jurisdiction case handling on the basis of computer network construction.

III. Construction Principles

The principles for the construction of computer information network systems of people's courts are unified leadership, unified planning, and unified standards, with organized and planned implementation, avoiding low-level redundant construction.

(1) Unified leadership. The construction of computer information network systems of people's courts shall be carried out under the unified leadership of the Supreme People's Court. Higher-level people's courts shall strengthen their leadership and guidance over the network construction work of lower-level courts. Leaders of people's courts at all levels must fully recognize the importance and urgency of constructing computer information networks of people's courts, strengthen leadership over the construction of computer information network systems, organize capable management and technical teams, secure construction funds, formulate specific measures, and, in accordance with the requirements of the Supreme People's Court, formulate and implement construction plans. They shall promptly pursue system construction and attach importance to system application.

(2) Unified planning. The construction and application of computer information network systems of people's courts is a systematic project involving a wide range of areas and intensive technology and capital. To ensure the system achieves overall benefits, it shall be constructed jointly and developed together by people's courts at all levels under the guidance of unified planning by the Supreme People's Court, in compliance with unified specifications and standards. Each high people's court shall formulate as soon as possible a plan for the construction of computer information networks of people's courts within its jurisdiction and earnestly organize its implementation. Special attention shall be paid to the practicality and effectiveness of system construction so that construction funds and information resources can yield greater benefits.

In accordance with the relevant requirements of the Supreme People's Court's administrative provisions on the construction of computer information networks of people's courts, a computer network construction plan may only be implemented after approval, and a computer network system may only be connected to the network after passing acceptance.

(3) Unified standards. To ensure the smooth progress of the construction of computer information network systems of people's courts and to provide convenient and simple basic conditions for WAN interconnection and network management, the Supreme People's Court issued in 2001 various technical standards for the construction of computer information network systems, including network basic functions, business flow modes and data exchange with higher and lower courts, basic data structures, judicial statistics interfaces, standard code tables, etc. People's courts at all levels must strictly implement various technical standards in the construction of computer information networks and shall not act independently.

(4) Emphasis on network security. Measures and systems for safety and confidentiality in the construction of computer information network systems of people's courts shall be formulated and improved, and a system of responsibility for safety and confidentiality work shall be implemented. Courts at all levels shall adopt confidentiality technologies that have been reviewed and certified by the competent state authorities to ensure the security of the court system's computer network. The safety and confidentiality system for WAN interconnection between the Supreme People's Court and high people's courts shall be constructed uniformly by the Supreme People's Court with the cooperation of the competent state safety and confidentiality authorities. The safety and confidentiality system for WAN interconnection between high people's courts and intermediate and basic people's courts in each province, autonomous region, and municipality directly under the Central Government shall be organized and constructed by the high people's court with the assistance of relevant safety and confidentiality departments.

State safety and confidentiality laws and regulations shall be strictly observed, and effective measures shall be taken to ensure the security of state secrets.

(5) Combination of centralized development and universal construction. Each high people's court may, based on local circumstances and in accordance with the technical standards for network application software, uniformly develop software within its jurisdiction. Hardware systems shall be configured in accordance with the requirements of the unified application software and system tasks to accelerate the construction progress.

IV. Main Tasks

To achieve the overall task objectives of the construction of computer information network systems of people's courts and to accelerate the process of construction and application, the following main tasks shall be completed during the Tenth Five-Year Plan period.

(1) Vigorously promote the construction of computer networks. Before the end of 2003, all higher people's courts and intermediate people's courts shall basically complete the construction of local area networks (LANs), pass acceptance inspection, and interconnect with the wide area network (WAN) of the Supreme People's Court. Before the end of 2005, basic people's courts shall basically complete the construction of LANs, pass acceptance inspection, and interconnect with the WAN of the Supreme People's Court. People's courts with the conditions may carry out construction ahead of schedule. For people's courts in underdeveloped central and western regions and those with poor economic conditions, the construction of computer information networks shall proceed from actual circumstances, and the network functions and scale may be determined based on funding conditions, but their basic functions shall first be realized. Basic people's courts in particularly impoverished areas may use a single computer to connect to the network of the superior court.

(2) In 2001, the Supreme People's Court shall complete the development of the "Supreme People's Court Information System" and the "People's Court Judicial Statistics System." Starting from 2002, people's courts at all levels nationwide shall use the new version of the "People's Court Judicial Statistics System." The database structure, inter-table data validation rules, and code tables of the "People's Court Judicial Statistics System" shall be disclosed to the court system. Courts that have already established computer network systems shall, in accordance with the technical standards issued by the Supreme People's Court and the requirements of the new version of the judicial statistics "Case Management Information Form," complete the upgrading and transformation of current application software in cooperation with partners, so as to facilitate interconnection with the WAN of the Supreme People's Court.

(3) At the beginning of 2003, a 2M data dedicated line shall be opened from the Supreme People's Court to higher people's courts, using digital multiplexing technology to realize the functions of dedicated telephone lines, wireless communication command and dispatch, computer networking, and image transmission on the dedicated data line, achieving "three networks in one." Encryption equipment shall be installed at both ends of the 2M data dedicated line to ensure safe and reliable data transmission. The 2M data dedicated line expands the dedicated line bandwidth, improves the call capacity of the dedicated telephone line, ensures the bandwidth of the computer networking channel, and increases the image transmission capacity, enabling the holding of video and telephone conferences and the transmission of trial site images and other image information. The method of dedicated lines for network connection by higher people's courts to lower courts shall be planned and designed by each higher people's court based on its funding capacity and local communication facilities, and shall be reported to the Supreme People's Court for filing.

(4) Starting in 2002, the construction of a paperless transmission system for official documents and trial information shall begin. Led by the Supreme People's Court, relying on technologies such as electronic authentication, electronic seals, and digital signatures, the system shall gradually realize paperless transmission of meeting notices, formal official documents, leadership speeches, work briefings, and the like.

(5) Actively prepare for the construction of the People's Court Public Information Website. To ensure fair adjudication and to guarantee effective public supervision over the work of the people's courts, during the "Tenth Five-Year Plan" period, people's courts with the conditions shall build court websites to publicly publish judgment documents in cases tried publicly.

People's courts at all levels shall strengthen the management of litigation archives and document archives, improve the level of archives management in the people's courts, gradually realize the electronic storage of archival media, facilitate the use of archives, and enhance management standards.

V. Safeguard Measures

The construction and application of the computer information network system of the people's courts is a long-term task. During the construction process, effective safeguard measures must be formulated to ensure the healthy and orderly development of this work.

(1) Leaders of people's courts at all levels shall attach importance to the construction and application of the computer information network system, conscientiously implement the regulations on the management of computer information network construction, strengthen supervision and inspection, increase coordination and guidance efforts, improve institutions, and staff positions adequately.

(2) To ensure the smooth progress of network construction, people's courts at all levels must have a dedicated technical team. People's courts with the conditions shall establish corresponding institutions. Training shall be targeted at management and technical personnel at different application levels, combining the characteristics of the construction and application of the people's courts' computer information network system, with the aim of forming a high-quality management and technical team within three to five years.

(3) For hardware system construction and software development in network construction, social forces shall be fully utilized. People's courts with the conditions shall engage computer experts as advisors for the construction of the computer information network system to guide and assist the court's network construction work.

(4) The construction of the computer information network system of the people's courts is a major project in the "National Tenth Five-Year Plan Period People's Court Material Construction Plan." People's courts at all levels shall attach importance to the funding input for the construction and application of the computer information network system of the people's courts, and ensure that construction funds are appropriated. According to relevant regulations, the funds required for computer network construction of people's courts at all levels shall be disbursed from the operational funds. People's courts at all levels shall make a budget for the required expenditure based on the actual needs of network construction and shall strengthen the management of construction funds.

(5) Superior courts shall strengthen their guidance over the computer network construction work of subordinate courts. Based on the progress of network construction in courts at all levels, various meetings shall be convened from time to time to organize research, exchange, and promote advanced experience. The Supreme People's Court shall issue a quarterly "Bulletin on the Construction of the Computer Information Network System of the People's Courts." Higher people's courts shall promptly report the status of computer information network construction to the Supreme People's Court, make full use of the "Bulletin on the Construction of the Computer Information Network System of the People's Courts," increase the publicity and guidance efforts for system construction, unify thinking, exchange experiences, discuss plans, promote mutual progress, and enhance improvement together.
